edges.description: Hyperglycosylated alpha-dystroglycan turns over faster, lowering its abundance.
Mannose restriction prevents neuron degeneration in the knockout, which ties neuron loss to the mannose excess; the intermediate steps are not described.
Correcting alpha-dystroglycan abundance by mannose restriction also normalizes muscle morphology in the knockout, tying the myopathy to the alpha-dystroglycan defect.
Myopathy is the tissue correlate of the muscle weakness reported in the syndrome.
Preventing neuron degeneration by mannose restriction also prevents the motor deficits in the knockout.
Cortical layering and cognitive performance persist together after dietary rescue, consistent with the cortical defect underlying the cognitive phenotype.
Absent tear production is attributed to autonomic dysfunction.
Achalasia is counted among the autonomic features.
The same alpha-dystroglycan hyperglycosylation is found in mouse and human tissue.
edges.limitations: The model is characterized for its neuromuscular and cognitive features; tear production and esophageal motility, the two features present in every patient, are not among the phenotypes described for it.

edges.description: The knockout develops myopathic alterations and motor deficits.

evidence.reference_title: Cryo-EM structures of human GMPPA-GMPPB complex reveal how cells maintain GDP-mannose homeostasis.
evidence.snippet: Unexpectedly, we find that the catalytically inactive subunit GMPPA displays a much higher affinity to GDP-Man than the active subunit GMPPB and, subsequently, inhibits the catalytic activity of GMPPB through a unique C-terminal loop of GMPPA.

nodes.description: Abnormal cortical layering in the knockout mouse. It is not corrected by mannose restriction from weaning, together with cognitive performance, which suggests it arises earlier in development. Its link to the GDP-mannose excess is not shown directly, so it has no upstream edge.

evidence.reference_title: GMPPA defects cause a neuromuscular disorder with α-dystroglycan hyperglycosylation.

nodes.description: Experimental and so far only in mice. Restricting dietary mannose from weaning corrected alpha-dystroglycan hyperglycosylation, muscle morphology and neuron loss in Gmppa knockout mice, but not cortical layering or cognition.
